# `silk/machine/chart`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Statecharts written as a static table over union types: [`Chart`](#Chart) and [`Machine`](#Machine).

## When to use
Use this module to describe behavior that depends on a state: a download that retries, a form
with steps, a connection that opens and closes. Write the states as a union, the events as a
union, and implement [`Machine`](#Machine) for the state union with a [`Chart`](#Chart) that connects them. Use
the `silk.machine.simple` module when the machine keeps no data and queues no effects.

## Details
A chart row names the state it leaves and the event it takes, and the compiler checks both
names against the unions. The state a row enters is a value of the state union, so a state can
hold data. A machine never performs work: `enter`, `exit` and `handle` queue effects as values
through [`Enqueue`](#Enqueue), and the caller performs them. Guards are built with [`Guards`](#Guards). A field of
a state that holds a machine of its own is a region, declared with [`Chart.region`](#Chart.impl.region).

## Gotchas
Rows for one state and event are tried in the order they are written. Put a guarded row before
the plain row for the same state and event.

Import as `Chart` with `import silk.machine.chart { Chart }`.

Public declarations: 25.

<a id="Guards"></a>

## `Guards`

```silk
pub struct Guards
```

Builds guards out of several functions for [`Chart.onWhen`](#Chart.impl.onWhen) and the other `When` builders.

### When to use
Use it when a transition depends on more than one check, so each check stays a small
function that can be named and reused:
`Guards.and(Guards.of(isPaid), Guards.not(Guards.of(isLocked)))`. A `When` builder takes
such a guard or one function directly.

### Details
The functions of one guard all have the contract of the place the guard is used:
`fn(&C, &E) -> bool` on a transition that takes an event, `fn(&C) -> bool` on an eventless
one. A function with another contract is a compile error where the chart is used. `and`
and `or` stop at the first part that decides the answer, in the order written.

<a id="Chart.impl.on"></a>

### Associated function `on`

```silk
pub static fn on(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    target: S,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Adds a transition: in the state named `state`, the event named `event` takes the machine
to `target`.

#### Details
`state` and `event` are names, because a transition leaves a state and takes an event
whatever their fields hold. `target` is a value of the state union, so it gives the
fields of the state it enters: its data, and the state of each of its regions. This holds
for the target of every kind of transition.

A transition between two values of one state runs no exit and no entry function of that
state, only those of the regions that changed.

<a id="Chart.impl.refuse"></a>

### Associated function `refuse`

```silk
pub static fn refuse(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    reason: string<'static>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Makes `state` refuse `event` for the reason `reason`: the state takes the event, changes
nothing, and the states above it do not get the event.

#### When to use
Use it for a command that must fail in this state and leave everything as it was, such as
removing something that is not there. A [`Chart.leaves`](#Chart.impl.leaves) after the row gives what the
refusal leaves behind, such as a message and an exit status.

#### Details
When the machine runs, a refusal is a [`Chart.stay`](#Chart.impl.stay). The difference is for people and for
tools that read the chart: the `Definition` keeps `reason`, so a refused event is told
apart from one nobody wrote a row for.

<a id="Chart.impl.refuseWhen"></a>

### Associated function `refuseWhen`

```silk
pub static fn refuseWhen<G>(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    guard: G,
    reason: string<'static>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Makes `state` refuse `event` for the reason `reason` when `guard` holds: the state takes
the event and changes nothing. `guard` is a function `fn(&C, &E) -> bool` or a [`Guard`](#Guard).
The `Definition` of the machine keeps `reason`.

<a id="Chart.impl.leaves"></a>

### Associated function `leaves`

```silk
pub static fn leaves(chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>, effects: &[X]) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Gives the row declared just before it the effects it leaves: when the machine takes the
row, it queues `effects` in order.

#### When to use
Use it to say in the chart what a transition does, so a reader, a generated page and a
test can all see it: `Chart.on("Idle", "Start", Job.Running) |> Chart.leaves(&[...])`.
Effects queued in `Machine.enter`, `Machine.exit` and `Machine.handle` are code, and
only the running machine sees them.

#### Details
The row is the last one added with a builder that adds a transition: `on`, `stay`,
`refuse`, `resume`, `always`, `onDone`, `after` and their `When` forms. A second
`leaves` for one row adds to the first. The effects are queued after the exit functions
of the states the row leaves and before the entry functions of the states it enters.
A row without a target queues them and changes no state. For each effect the machine
first calls `Machine.absorb`, so the context can take in what the effect means. The
`Definition` of the machine keeps the effects as text.

#### Gotchas
It is a compile error when the chart has no row yet.

<a id="Chart.impl.awaits"></a>

### Associated function `awaits`

```silk
pub static fn awaits(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Says that `state` waits for the world to answer, and that `event` is one of the answers.

#### When to use
Use it for a state that stands for work in progress whose result the machine cannot
know, such as a download that arrives or is cut. Call it one time for each answer. A
program that runs the machine does the work when the machine rests in the state, and
sends the answer. A tool that walks the machine tries every answer of the state and no
other event there.

#### Details
It adds no transition: each answer still needs its row. `Machines.awaiting` tells
whether an active state waits for an answer, and `Machines.awaits` whether it waits for
one event.

<a id="Chart.impl.metaOn"></a>

### Associated function `metaOn`

```silk
pub static fn metaOn(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    key: string<'static>,
    value: string<'static>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Gives the transition that `event` takes in `state` the meta data `value` under `key`:
static text about the transition for tools that read the chart, such as a label for a
diagram or a note for a test generator.

#### Details
The meta data goes to the last transition declared so far for `state` and `event`, so
write it right after the row it describes. When a state has a guarded row and a plain row
for one event, each one takes its own. It is a compile error when no row was declared.
The meta data is part of the `Definition` of the machine and of its xstate config. It is
not read while the machine runs: for that, give the target state a [`Chart.meta`](#Chart.impl.meta).

<a id="Chart.impl.history"></a>

### Associated function `history`

```silk
pub static fn history(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    field: Intrinsic.FieldName<C>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Keeps the value of `state`, with its regions, in the context field `field` when the chart
leaves the state. The field is a `History<S>`. A transition added with [`Chart.resume`](#Chart.impl.resume)
enters the state as it was, which is xstate's deep history.

#### Details
The kept value is a copy of the state, so the data fields of the states of a chart with a
history, and of the regions below them, must be `Copy`.

The value is kept whenever the state is left: when this chart leaves it, and when a parent
state that holds this chart as a region is left.

<a id="Chart.impl.shallowHistory"></a>

### Associated function `shallowHistory`

```silk
pub static fn shallowHistory(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    field: Intrinsic.FieldName<C>,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Like [`Chart.history`](#Chart.impl.history), but a transition that comes back restores only the state of each
region, and the regions below those start at their initial states. This is xstate's
shallow history.

<a id="Chart.impl.resume"></a>

### Associated function `resume`

```silk
pub static fn resume(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    event: Intrinsic.VariantName<E>,
    target: S,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Adds a transition to the history of the state of `target`: the state is entered as it was
when the chart last left it, or as `target` when nothing is remembered. Entry functions
run for every state entered.

```silk
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

### Associated function `alwaysWhen`

```silk
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    target: S,
```

<a id="Chart.impl.onDone"></a>

### Associated function `onDone`

```silk
pub static fn onDone(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    target: S,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Adds a transition taken as soon as every region of `state` is in a final state of its
chart: the region of a compound state, or all the regions of a parallel state. This is
xstate's `onDone`.

#### Details
It is an eventless transition, tried after the [`Chart.always`](#Chart.impl.always) rows of the state. Its
target must leave the state's variant or start a region outside its final state, or the
machine never settles and the step fails with `TransitionLoopError`.

<a id="Chart.impl.after"></a>

### Associated function `after`

```silk
pub static fn after(
    chart: Chart<S, E, C, X>,
    state: Intrinsic.VariantName<S>,
    duration: u64,
    target: S,
  ) -> Chart<S, E, C, X>
```

Adds a delayed transition: after `duration` in `state`, the machine goes to `target`.
A duration is nanoseconds, so a duration literal such as `500ms` or `1m30s` gives one.
The timer starts when the state is entered and is cancelled when the state is left.

```silk
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

<a id="Machine.absorb"></a>

### Operation `absorb`

```silk
fn absorb(state: &Self, context: &mut C, effect_: &X) -> ()
```

Takes in an effect that a row of this chart leaves, before the effect is queued. The
default does nothing.

#### When to use
Implement it when the context is a model of what the effects change, so one function
says what each effect means for the context: an effect that creates a file marks the
file as present. It runs for the effects of [`Chart.leaves`](#Chart.impl.leaves) only, not for effects that
`enter`, `exit` and `handle` queue.

<a id="Machine.deadline"></a>

### Operation `deadline`

```silk
fn deadline(state: &Self, context: &C) -> Option<u64>
```

The next time something the context holds needs [`Machine.tick`](#Machine.tick), in nanoseconds of wall
clock time. A machine with a child returns the child's next deadline. The default has
none. Only the machine's own states are asked, not its regions.

<a id="Machine.tick"></a>

### Operation `tick`

```silk
effect fn tick(state: &Self, context: &mut C, now: u64, enq: &mut Enqueue<E, X>) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Runs when the clock reaches [`Machine.deadline`](#Machine.deadline). A machine with a child advances the
child to `now` here and moves its effects into `enq`. The default does nothing.

### Associated function `enterAll`

```silk
pub effect fn enterAll<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    state: &S,
    context: &mut C,
    enq: &mut Enqueue<E, X>,
  ) -> ()

```

Runs the entry functions of `state`, parents before children, and starts the timers of
the states entered.

<a id="Machines.impl.exitAll"></a>

### Associated function `exitAll`

```silk
pub effect fn exitAll<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    state: &S,
    context: &mut C,
    enq: &mut Enqueue<E, X>,
  ) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Runs the exit functions of `state`, children before parents, and cancels the timers of
the states left.

<a id="Machines.impl.dispatch"></a>

### Associated function `dispatch`

```silk
pub effect fn dispatch<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    state: &mut S,
    context: &mut C,
    event: &E,
    enq: &mut Enqueue<E, X>,
  ) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Offers `event` to `state`, deepest states first, and returns whether a state handled it.

#### Details
The step has two passes, as an xstate microstep does. The first one picks, in every
active state, the declared transition the event takes, so every guard sees the context
as it was before the event. The second one takes them, deepest states first, with their
exit and entry functions. `Machine.handle` runs in the second pass, before the declared
transitions of its state, so it sees what the states below it and the regions before it
changed. A final state takes no events.

<a id="Machines.impl.awaiting"></a>

### Associated function `awaiting`

```silk
pub fn awaiting<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(state: &S) -> bool
```

Returns whether an active state of `state`, at any depth, waits for an answer of the
world: its chart names it in a [`Chart.awaits`](#Chart.impl.awaits).

<a id="Machines.impl.awaits"></a>

### Associated function `awaits`

```silk

```

Returns whether an active state of `state`, at any depth, waits for `event` as an answer
of the world: its chart names the state and the variant of `event` in a
[`Chart.awaits`](#Chart.impl.awaits).

<a id="Machines.impl.isAnswer"></a>

### Associated function `isAnswer`

```silk
pub fn isAnswer<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(event: &E) -> bool
```

Returns whether a state of the machine `S`, at any depth, waits for `event` as an answer
of the world: a chart of the machine names the variant of `event` in a [`Chart.awaits`](#Chart.impl.awaits).
The states that are active do not matter.

<a id="Machines.impl.active"></a>

### Associated function `active`

```silk
pub effect fn active<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    state: &S,
    names: &mut List<string<'static>>,
  ) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends to `names` the name of every active state of `state`, parents before children.
A name is the type of the chart and the state, as in `Door.Open`.

<a id="Machines.impl.states"></a>

### Associated function `states`

```silk
pub effect fn states<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(names: &mut List<string<'static>>) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends to `names` the name of every state of the machine `S`: the states of its chart,
then the states of the chart of each region. A name is the type of the chart and the
state, as in `Door.Open`. A chart that several states hold as a region is named each
time.

<a id="Machines.impl.contenders"></a>

### Associated function `contenders`

```silk
pub fn contenders<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(state: &S, context: &C, event: &E) -> u32
```

Returns the largest number of declared transitions that `event` could take in one active
state of `state`: the rows of that state for the event, or for any event, whose guards
hold.

#### When to use
A tool that checks a chart calls it to find rows that overlap. When the result is more
than 1, two rows of one state apply at once and the order they were written in decides
which one the machine takes. A final state counts as 0.

```silk
pub fn hasTag<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(state: &S, tag: string) -> bool
```

Returns whether an active state of `state`, at any depth, has the tag `tag`.

<a id="Machines.impl.meta"></a>

### Associated function `meta`

```silk

```

Returns the meta data under `key` of the active state of `state`. When that state has

<a id="Machines.impl.settle"></a>

### Associated function `settle`

```silk
pub effect fn settle<S: Machine<E, C, X>, E, C, X>(
    state: &mut S,
    context: &mut C,
    enq: &mut Enqueue<E, X>,
  ) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Takes one enabled eventless transition, and returns whether it took one.

#### Details
The regions of the active state come first, deepest first, then the state's own
transitions: its [`Chart.always`](#Chart.impl.always) rows, then its [`Chart.onDone`](#Chart.impl.onDone) rows, which are taken
when every region of the state is in a final state.

```silk
  ) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError

```

Takes the delayed transition `index` of the chart at `path`, if its state is active, and
returns whether it was taken. `path` is the one the timer was started with.
